title: a Layer.provide callback runs, so ambient host authority read inside one is part of the pinned graph
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Scoping': '`Layer.provide(layer, body)` MUST keep its environment active through `body` and the Promise returned by `body`, then revoke it.' Keeping an environment active THROUGH a body is a statement that the body runs, so what it reads is reachable. specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin': the assertion is over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE GRAPH and 'any reachable operation'. An analysis that stops at the provide site never looks inside the callback, and the consequence is the fail-open direction: a pin GRANTED over a live `process` read one keyword away. The provided capability is deliberately unrelated to the read, which is the point — `Layer.provide` establishes a nominal context row and nothing about it makes ambient host authority portable. `messageContains` pins the route because a pin refused with an EMPTY route satisfies a code-and-position expectation exactly; here the route is the pinned function itself, which is what says the requirement was attributed to `scoped` rather than merely observed somewhere in the file. Read this case with 21-native-pin/a-layer-provided-capability-is-subtracted-and-the-pin-still-holds, which is the over-correction guard: entering the callback is only half the rule, and an implementation that reported everything it found inside a provide would satisfy this case and fail that one. The SMITHERS1601 companion is 20-host-globals/host-globals-are-unavailable's rule at the ambient read, declared rather than filtered because a cascade the language really does produce is part of the contract. Both backends refuse it today, so this case pins current behaviour on both rather than reproducing a live one-sided defect; the historical defect was the reference's and reverting poc/src/targets/classify.ts is another lane's work.
